title: Mock 7 · Final Simulation
blurb: A last full-strength rehearsal: harder corpus and tax sums, NPS edge cases, regulator rules and close distractors.

questions.q: X invests either ₹5,000 every month or ₹60,000 once a year for 30 years, earning 12% a year in both cases. Which is correct, according to the workbook's illustration?
options: Both give exactly the same corpus since the total invested is the same
Monthly investing gives a larger corpus (about ₹1.75 crore vs ₹1.45 crore) because of more frequent compounding
Monthly investing gives a smaller corpus because of higher transaction costs
Annual investing gives a larger corpus because the lump sum earns more
questions.explanation: Box 1.3: ₹5,000 a month for 360 months at 12%/12 grows to about ₹1,74,74,820, while ₹60,000 a year for 30 years at 12% grows to about ₹1,44,79,961. More frequent compounding gives a higher final value.
hints: Wrong: the same total contribution does not mean the same corpus.
Correct: monthly compounding wins.
Wrong: costs are not the point of the illustration.
Wrong: the annual plan grows less.

questions.q: If consumer prices rise 6% a year, an item costing ₹100 today will cost approximately how much in 20 years?
questions.explanation: ₹100 × 1.06^20 ≈ ₹321. The workbook also gives ₹179 after 10 years and ₹574 after 30 years.
hints: Wrong: ₹179 is the 10-year figure.
Wrong: this is simple growth (100 + 6 × 20).
Wrong: ₹574 is the 30-year figure.

questions.q: Which statement about Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) is NOT correct as per the workbook?
options: REIT units trade in a minimum lot of 100 units
A full valuation of assets is done every year and updated every six months
At least 80% of the value of REIT assets must be in completed, rent-generating properties
The minimum application value in an initial offer is ₹10,000-15,000
questions.explanation: Following SEBI's 2021 amendments, REIT units trade in a lot of a single unit; the 100-unit lot applied earlier. The other statements are correct.
hints: Correct (this is the false statement): the trading lot is now 1 unit.
Wrong choice: annual valuation with a half-yearly update is correct.
Wrong choice: the 80% rule is correct.
Wrong choice: the minimum application value was reduced to ₹10,000-15,000.

questions.q: Which investment has NO market risk but is still exposed to inflation and reinvestment risk?
options: A gold ETF
A listed 10-year government bond
A 5-year post office time deposit
An equity index fund
questions.explanation: Deposits and small savings schemes are not marketable securities, so they carry no market risk, but fixed returns expose them to inflation risk and maturity proceeds to reinvestment risk.
hints: Wrong: gold ETF prices move with the market.
Wrong: listed bonds have price (market) risk from interest rate changes.
Correct: not marketable, fixed return.
Wrong: equity funds carry market risk.

questions.q: An arbitrage fund buys a share in the cash market at ₹80 and simultaneously sells it in the futures market at ₹100, holding both positions to expiry. What risk profile does the workbook attribute to such funds?
options: Very high risk, because derivatives are leveraged
High risk, similar to a mid-cap equity fund
Moderate risk, similar to a long-duration gilt fund
Low risk, with NAV volatility similar to a liquid fund
questions.explanation: The price differential is locked in if positions are held to expiry; a completely hedged position makes these funds low risk, with NAV volatility similar to a liquid fund.
hints: Wrong: the hedge removes directional risk.
Wrong: the position is hedged, unlike a mid-cap fund.
Wrong: long-duration gilt funds have much higher rate risk.
Correct: fully hedged, low volatility.

questions.q: Lata will need ₹1,00,000 a month at the start of a 25-year retirement (already inflation-adjusted to that date). Her corpus will earn 8% and inflation is 6%. Withdrawals are at the beginning of each month. Approximately what corpus does she need?
options: ₹2.36 crore
₹3.00 crore
₹1.30 crore
₹2.39 crore
hints: Wrong: this uses the approximate 2% real rate.
Wrong: this is 1 lakh × 300 with no discounting.
Wrong: this discounts at the nominal 8%, ignoring rising expenses.
Correct: discounting at the precise real rate.

questions.q: A client spends ₹60,000 a month today and retires in 20 years. Inflation is 6%. She plans a 30-year retirement with 20% equity (SWR 3.79% from the table). What corpus is required?
options: About ₹6.09 crore
About ₹6.13 crore
About ₹23.09 lakh
About ₹1.90 crore
hints: Correct: inflate first, annualise, then divide by the SWR.
Wrong: this uses 3.77% (0% equity) instead of 3.79%.
Wrong: this is only the first-year annual withdrawal.
Wrong: this uses today's expense without inflating it.

questions.q: Rahul needs ₹2 crore in 15 years. He already has ₹20 lakh in equity funds earmarked for retirement, expected to earn 10% a year. His new SIPs will earn 12% (monthly compounding, month-end). Approximately what monthly SIP does he need?
hints: Wrong: this does not follow from the PMT calculation.
Correct: deduct the future value of existing assets, then PMT.
Wrong: this deducts the current value (₹20 lakh) instead of its future value.
Wrong: this ignores the existing investment.

questions.q: A retiree with ₹1 crore adopts a 3.5% safe withdrawal rate and withdraws ₹3.5 lakh in year 1. Inflation is 6%. During year 1 the market falls and the corpus drops to ₹90 lakh. What should the year-2 withdrawal be under the SWR approach?
questions.explanation: Under SWR, the rupee withdrawal is raised by inflation each year independent of the corpus value: 3,50,000 × 1.06 = ₹3,71,000. The SWR is not a percentage applied to the corpus every year.
hints: Wrong: this applies 3.71% to ₹90 lakh, mixing the two ideas.
Wrong: this ignores the inflation adjustment.
Correct: indexed to inflation regardless of the corpus value.
Wrong: this applies 3.5% to the fallen corpus, which is not how SWR works.

questions.q: For a young earner whose income just about covers expenses, what should have the first claim on savings?
options: Annuity purchase for future income
A home loan to build an asset early
An emergency or reserve fund
Aggressive mid-cap equity for retirement
questions.explanation: At the young earner stage, creating an emergency or reserve fund to manage any loss or reduction in income should have first claim on savings; a long-term EMI commitment can be risky without income stability.
hints: Wrong: annuities are a distribution-stage product.
Wrong: the workbook warns that a long-term EMI without income stability is risky.
Correct: emergency fund first.
Wrong: long-term savings can go to equity, but not before the emergency fund.

questions.q: Mr Kapoor joined NPS under the All Citizen model at 62. At 67 he exits with a corpus of ₹11 lakh. What can he do?
options: Withdraw the entire ₹11 lakh as lump sum or through SLW/SUR
He cannot exit until he completes 15 years in NPS
Take up to ₹6 lakh as lump sum and annuitise the rest
Take up to 60% as lump sum and annuitise 40%
questions.explanation: For subscribers joining after 60, there is no vesting period; where the corpus is up to ₹12 lakh, the entire corpus may be withdrawn as lump sum or through approved systematic withdrawal options.
hints: Correct: the ₹12 lakh threshold applies to those joining after 60.
Wrong: the vesting period has been removed for those joining after 60.
Wrong: the ₹6 lakh rule applies to the ₹8-12 lakh slab for regular joiners.
Wrong: 60:40 applies to Government subscribers.

questions.q: A Central Government NPS subscriber retires on superannuation with a corpus of ₹10 lakh. Which option is NOT available?
options: Withdraw up to ₹6 lakh as lump sum and use the balance through SUR for at least six years
Withdraw the entire ₹10 lakh as lump sum
Withdraw up to 60% as lump sum and use at least 40% for an annuity
Withdraw up to ₹6 lakh as lump sum and use the balance for an annuity
questions.explanation: For a corpus of more than ₹8 lakh and up to ₹12 lakh, the subscriber may take up to ₹6 lakh lump sum with the balance in an annuity or SUR (minimum 6 years), or follow 60:40. Full withdrawal is allowed only up to ₹8 lakh.
hints: Wrong choice: the ₹6 lakh plus SUR route is available.
Correct (not available): full withdrawal requires a corpus up to ₹8 lakh.
Wrong choice: the standard 60:40 route is available.
Wrong choice: the ₹6 lakh plus annuity route is available.

questions.q: A private-sector employee under the OLD tax regime has Basic + DA of ₹12 lakh. His employer contributes 14% (₹1.68 lakh) to his NPS account. How much of the employer contribution is deductible under section 124(1) (old 80CCD(2))?
questions.explanation: For non-Government employees, the employer contribution is deductible up to 10% of salary: 10% × ₹12 lakh = ₹1.2 lakh. The 14% limit applies to Government employees and to all employees under the new regime.
hints: Wrong: ₹1.5 lakh is the s.123 aggregate limit.
Wrong: ₹50,000 is the s.124(3) limit on own contribution.
Wrong: 14% applies only under the new regime or for Government employees.
Correct: 10% of salary for a private employee under the old regime.

questions.q: In a year, an employer contributes ₹3 lakh to an employee's recognised PF, ₹4 lakh to NPS and ₹1.5 lakh to an approved superannuation fund. How much is taxable as a perquisite (ignoring accretions)?
options: Nil
questions.explanation: The aggregate employer contribution to recognised PF, NPS and approved superannuation fund is capped at ₹7.5 lakh a year. Total = ₹8.5 lakh, so ₹1 lakh is a taxable perquisite.
hints: Wrong: the total exceeds the ₹7.5 lakh cap.
Wrong: only the excess over ₹7.5 lakh is taxed.
Wrong: this treats the superannuation contribution as the excess.
Correct: ₹8.5 lakh − ₹7.5 lakh.

questions.q: Two subscribers aged 50 are in Auto choice: Asha in Life Cycle – Aggressive and Bina in Life Cycle 50 (Moderate). What are their equity allocations?
options: Asha 50%, Bina 30%
Asha 40%, Bina 20%
Asha 20%, Bina 40%
Asha 35%, Bina 10%
questions.explanation: At age 50, LC Aggressive holds 40/20/40 (E/C/G) and LC50 holds 20/15/65.
hints: Wrong: these are the levels at about age 45 (Aggressive holds 50% until 45; LC50 is 30% at 45).
Correct: 40% and 20%.
Wrong: the values are swapped.
Wrong: these are the terminal levels at 55 and above.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a function of a Central Recordkeeping Agency under NPS?
options: Providing a centralised grievance management system
Computing and declaring scheme NAV on a daily basis
Issuing the PRAN, I-PIN and T-PIN
Processing exit and withdrawal requests
questions.explanation: Computing and declaring scheme NAV daily is a function of the Pension Fund. Issuing PRAN, running grievance systems and processing exits are CRA functions.
hints: Wrong choice: the CRA provides the grievance system.
Correct (not a CRA function): Pension Funds compute NAV.
Wrong choice: the CRA issues PRAN, I-PIN and T-PIN.
Wrong choice: the CRA processes exits and withdrawals.

questions.q: A fund gained 18% in 9 months. What is its simple annualised return using the workbook's method?
questions.explanation: Annualised return = absolute return × (12/months held) = 18% × 12/9 = 24%.
hints: Wrong: this is the absolute return.
Wrong: this does not follow the formula.
Correct: 18 × 12/9.
Wrong: this multiplies by 9/12 instead of 12/9.

questions.q: An investor holds a debenture of face value ₹100 with a 9% coupon. During the year its market price falls to ₹97. What is the total return for the year?
questions.explanation: Total return = interest income + change in value = ₹9 + (97 − 100) = ₹6.
hints: Wrong: this adds the price fall instead of subtracting it.
Correct: 9 − 3.
Wrong: this is the capital loss only.
Wrong: this is the coupon only.

questions.q: A fund has a beta of 0.8. If the market index falls 15%, the fund is expected to:
options: Fall about 12%
Fall about 15%
Rise about 12%
Fall about 18.75%
questions.explanation: Expected move = beta × market move = 0.8 × (−15%) = −12%. A beta below 1 means less volatility than the market.
hints: Correct: 0.8 × −15%.
Wrong: that would be a beta of 1.
Wrong: a positive beta moves in the same direction as the market.
Wrong: this divides by beta.

questions.q: In a financial year, an employee contributes ₹3.5 lakh (EPF + VPF) and the employer also contributes to his provident fund. Interest on what portion of his own contribution is taxable?
options: Interest on ₹1 lakh
Interest on ₹3 lakh
Interest on the full ₹3.5 lakh
No interest is taxable
questions.explanation: Interest on the employee's own contribution up to ₹2.5 lakh a year is tax-free; interest on the excess (₹3.5 lakh − ₹2.5 lakh = ₹1 lakh) is taxable. The ₹5 lakh threshold applies only where there is no employer contribution.
hints: Correct: the excess over ₹2.5 lakh.
Wrong: this would apply a ₹50,000 threshold.
Wrong: interest on the first ₹2.5 lakh is tax-free.
Wrong: the contribution exceeds ₹2.5 lakh.

questions.q: Which statement about the Public Provident Fund is NOT correct?
options: The maximum deposit is ₹1.5 lakh in a financial year
A Hindu Undivided Family can open a PPF account
The account has a tenure of 15 years
Interest earned and the maturity value are tax-free
questions.explanation: PPF can be opened by individuals only; HUFs and NRIs cannot open a PPF account. The other statements are correct.
hints: Wrong choice: ₹1.5 lakh is the annual maximum.
Correct (this is the false statement): HUFs cannot open PPF.
Wrong choice: PPF is a 15-year account.
Wrong choice: PPF is EEE.

questions.q: For the same purchase price, which annuity is likely to give the HIGHEST periodic payout?
options: Life annuity without return of purchase price, bought by a 75-year-old man in poor health
Joint-life annuity with 100% to spouse, bought at 60
Life annuity increasing at 3% simple, bought at 60
Life annuity with return of purchase price, bought by a 60-year-old woman
questions.explanation: Add-on features (return of purchase price, spouse cover, increasing payouts) lower the payout. Older age, male gender and poor health shorten life expectancy, which raises the payout.
hints: Correct: no add-ons, high age, male and poor health all raise the payout.
Wrong: spouse cover lowers the payout.
Wrong: the step-up feature lowers the starting payout.
Wrong: ROP and female life expectancy lower the payout.

questions.q: An investor puts ₹1,000 each month for three months into a fund at NAVs of ₹10, ₹12.50 and ₹8. What is his average cost per unit?
options: About ₹9.84
questions.explanation: Units = 100 + 80 + 125 = 305. Average cost = ₹3,000 ÷ 305 ≈ ₹9.84, lower than the simple average NAV of ₹10.17. This is rupee-cost averaging.
hints: Wrong: this is the lowest NAV, which averaging does not achieve.
Wrong: this is the simple average of the three NAVs.
Correct: total invested ÷ total units.
Wrong: this is the first NAV only.

questions.q: A retiree's taxable income is ₹10.5 lakh, which would push part of it into a higher tax slab. How does the workbook suggest tax-free income can help?
options: Use tax-free income, such as interest from tax-free bonds, to meet the last ₹50,000 so taxable income stays in the lower slab
Use a reverse mortgage lump sum to pay the tax
Withdraw extra from the NPS annuity, which is tax-free
Convert all income to tax-free bonds regardless of yield
questions.explanation: If the retiree has access to tax-free income, it can bridge the last ₹50,000 required so that taxable income stays within the lower bracket.
hints: Correct: tax-free income prevents tipping into the next slab.
Wrong: this is not the strategy described.
Wrong: annuity income is taxable.
Wrong: the choice depends on returns and the tax bracket.

questions.q: Under the NPS Retirement Income Scheme 'RIS Steady', what is the equity exposure of a subscriber aged 80 in drawdown?
questions.explanation: RIS Steady reduces equity from 35% at age 60 to a floor of 10% at age 75, held constant thereafter until 85.
hints: Wrong: 35% is the starting equity at 60.
Wrong: the floor is 10%, not zero.
Correct: 10% from 75 to 85.
Wrong: not a level in the RIS Steady glide path at 80.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT an essential requirement for a valid will as listed in the workbook?
options: Attestation by two witnesses
Signature of the testator
Clear listing of the beneficiaries and property bequeathed
Registration with the sub-registrar
questions.explanation: It is not compulsory to register a will, though it is good practice. A will must be in writing, signed by the testator and attested by two witnesses, and should list beneficiaries and property.
hints: Wrong choice: two witnesses are required.
Wrong choice: the testator's signature is required.
Wrong choice: beneficiaries and property must be listed.
Correct (not essential): registration is optional.

questions.q: For how long can reassessment proceedings generally be initiated where the income that escaped assessment is ₹50 lakh or more, which guides how long ITR copies should be kept?
options: 5 years from the end of the relevant assessment year
Indefinitely
10 years from the end of the financial year
3 years from the end of the relevant assessment year
questions.explanation: Reassessment can generally be initiated within 3 years from the end of the relevant assessment year, extended to 5 years where escaped income is ₹50 lakh or more.
hints: Correct: 5 years for ₹50 lakh or more.
Wrong: there is a time limit.
Wrong: not the limit stated in the workbook.
Wrong: 3 years is the general limit.

questions.q: Which statement about a sponsor's obligations for a pension fund under the PFRDA (Pension Fund) Regulations is NOT correct?
options: The pension fund must maintain a net worth of ₹50 crore at all times
No director on a pension fund's board may be a director of another registered pension fund
The sponsor must not hold 20% or more equity in the CRA, custodian or trustee bank
At least 25% of the pension fund's directors must be independent directors
questions.explanation: At least 50% (not 25%) of the directors of the pension fund must be independent directors. The other statements are correct.
hints: Wrong choice: ₹50 crore net worth at all times is correct.
Wrong choice: cross-directorships across pension funds are barred.
Wrong choice: the 20% cross-holding restriction is correct.
Correct (this is the false statement): the requirement is at least 50%.

questions.q: An NPS subscriber who has a family nominates only a close friend. Under the nomination provisions of the Exit regulations, this nomination is:
options: Valid only if the friend is a minor with a guardian
Valid, since the subscriber may nominate anyone
Valid if registered with the Ombudsman
Invalid, because a subscriber with a family must nominate one or more family members
questions.explanation: If a subscriber has a family at the time of nomination, the nomination must be in favour of one or more family members; a nomination in favour of a non-family member is invalid.
hints: Wrong: being a minor does not change the family rule.
Wrong: this applies only if the subscriber has no family.
Wrong: nominations are not registered with the Ombudsman.
Correct: nomination must favour family members.

questions.q: For Government sector NPS subscribers, at what frequency must an empanelled Annuity Service Provider pay the annuity?
options: Monthly, quarterly or annually, as the subscriber chooses
Monthly only
Half-yearly only
Annually only
questions.explanation: The ASP delivers the monthly, quarterly or annual pension as chosen by the subscriber; however, for Government sector subscribers the annuity is payable on a monthly basis only.
hints: Wrong: the choice of frequency applies to non-Government subscribers.
Correct: monthly only for Government subscribers.
Wrong: not permitted for Government subscribers.
Wrong: not permitted for Government subscribers.
